answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it is accepted. Each square depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot divide one chain among clones or compute its steps in parallel; every additional identity therefore incurs its own real-time delay. Like a voyage paced by a sonnet’s measured lines, no amount of hardware lets an attacker wander past the sequential bottleneck.
